title: Official EU AI Act Sources — EU AI Act Toolkit
content: Official EU AI Act Sources — EU AI Act Toolkit 🇪🇺 "> 🇪🇺 EU AI Act Toolkit Core Actions Dashboard Toolkit Packs Use Cases Resources Interactive Tools Readiness Self-Check Industry Analyzer Risk Decision Tree Support & Info EU Sources Community Roadmap 🏛️ Authoritative EU Publications Official EU AI Act Sources Direct links to official EU publications, regulations, and authoritative guidance on the EU AI Act. Clearly separated from this toolkit's own materials. These links point to external official EU websites. This toolkit does not control or maintain those sites. ℹ️ About This Page This page provides curated links to official EU sources only. The EU AI Act Toolkit is an independent practical resource — it is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or produced by the European Union, European Commission, or any EU institution. Always consult the official sources for authoritative legal text and policy guidance. Primary Sources The Regulation and Its Official Text The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) is published on EUR-Lex, the official EU law database. 📜 Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 — Full Official Text The complete and authoritative text of the EU Artificial Intelligence Act as published in the Official Journal of the European Union. This is the primary legal source. Open on EUR-Lex ↗ EUR-Lex · Official Journal of the EU · Published 12 July 2024 📖 EUR-Lex Summary — Rules for Trustworthy AI The official EUR-Lex summary of the EU AI Act, providing a structured overview of the regulation's scope, provisions, and key concepts. Open Summary ↗ EUR-Lex · Legislative summary · Official EU overview 🔍 EUR-Lex Document Hub for 2024/1689 The main EUR-Lex entry for the AI Act regulation, including full text, related documents, language versions, and legislative history. Open on EUR-Lex ↗ CELEX: 32024R1689 · All language versions and related documents European Commission Commission Policy and Regulatory Framework Official policy pages from the European Commission on AI regulation and the EU AI Office. 🇪🇺 European Commission — AI Regulatory Framework The European Commission's official page on the EU AI Act regulatory framework, including policy context, key provisions, and implementation resources. Open on EC ↗ digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu · Official Commission policy page 🏢 European AI Office The EU AI Office is the official body responsible for overseeing the implementation of the AI Act, particularly for general-purpose AI models and cross-border cases. Open AI Office page ↗ digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu · EU AI Office official page 📊 European Commission — AI Policy Overview The broader EU digital strategy AI policy section, covering the Commission's overall approach to AI governance, ethics, and regulation. Open Policy Overview ↗ digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu · European approach to AI Key Concepts What the EU AI Act Covers A brief plain-language overview of the regulation's scope — for context only. Always refer to the official text. 🏗️ Risk-Based Framework The AI Act categorises AI systems by risk level: unacceptable risk (prohibited), high risk (strict requirements), limited risk (transparency), and minimal risk (general guidance). ⚠️ High-Risk AI Systems High-risk systems include those used in employment, education, critical infrastructure, law enforcement, access to services, and certain biometric applications. 🚫 Prohibited Practices Certain AI practices are prohibited entirely: social scoring by public authorities, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces (with narrow exceptions), and manipulation of vulnerable groups. 🤖 General Purpose AI The AI Act includes specific provisions for GPAI models (like large language models), with transparency and safety requirements for models of significant capability. 📅 Phased Application The AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024. Most obligations apply gradually — prohibited practices from early 2025, high-risk system rules from 2026, and full application by August 2027. 🔍 SME Considerations The regulation includes provisions for SMEs and start-ups, including regulatory sandboxes and proportionate obligations where possible — though substantive compliance requirements still apply. ⚠️ Simplified overview only The summary above is a simplified, non-exhaustive overview for orientation purposes. The official EUR-Lex text is the authoritative source. Consult a qualified legal professional for advice on your specific obligations. View Schema Frequently Asked Questions Common Questions Quick answers to the most common questions about the toolkit, readiness, and the EU AI Act. Does using this toolkit make my organisation compliant with the EU AI Act? No. This toolkit is educational and informational — it provides practical readiness support and documentation templates. It does not constitute legal advice and cannot guarantee or confirm compliance. Legal compliance determinations require qualified legal review specific to your organisation and use case. Who is this toolkit designed for? Primarily SMEs and teams working with AI tools who do not have dedicated legal or compliance staff. It is designed to be accessible to non-lawyers while remaining grounded in the official regulation and conservative interpretation. Does the EU AI Act apply to my organisation if we only use third-party AI tools? The EU AI Act applies to providers and deployers of AI systems. If you use AI-enabled SaaS tools in your operations, you may be a deployer under the regulation — which carries its own obligations, particularly for higher-risk use cases. The decision tree and escalation guide can help identify what attention your specific use warrants. When does the EU AI Act apply? The regulation entered into force on 1 August 2024. Provisions apply on a phased basis: prohibited practices from early 2025, GPAI model obligations from August 2025, high-risk system rules from August 2026, and full application by August 2027. Always verify current dates against the official text on EUR-Lex. Where should I start if I am new to this topic? Take the 2-minute AI governance self-check first. Then review the Starter Pack, starting with the 30-minute readiness self-assessment. The decision tree and FAQ are useful secondary references once you have a baseline sense of your situation. Is this toolkit affiliated with the EU or European Commission? No. The EU AI Act Toolkit is an independent resource maintained by Artem Nazarko. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or produced by the European Union, European Commission, or any EU institution. Official sources are linked on the EU Sources page. title: Compliance Roadmap
content: EU AI Act Toolkit — Compliance Roadmap 🇪🇺 EU AI Act Toolkit Dashboard Sector Packs Readiness Check Industry Analyzer Decision Tree Roadmap Resources Search Cmd+K EN ▾ FR (Soon) DE (Soon) Compliance Roadmap Interactive timeline of the EU AI Act enforcement milestones. ⏱️ EU AI Act Deadline Loading... -- Days -- Hours -- Mins -- Secs Switch Compliance Milestone ⇥ Interactive Regulatory Timeline Filter by specific compliance years or responsible actors to isolate critical deadlines. 📥 Download Original Timeline Infographic Filter by Regulatory Phase All Phases 2024 2025 2026 2027 2028 - 2031 Filter by Primary Subject All Subjects ⏱️ Application Scope 🇪🇺 EU Commission 🏛️ Member States 🏢 Businesses August 1, 2024 General Enforcement Regulatory Entry into Force The EU AI Act formally becomes active as a binding European regulation. While initial compliance duties are not yet mandatory, this sets the baseline calendar from which all staggered transitional timelines are officially calculated. Article 113 November 2, 2024 Member States Fundamental Rights Protection Mapping All EU Member States must identify and establish public authorities and agencies responsible for protecting fundamental human rights under the Act's provisions. These bodies must be declared to the EU Commission. Article 77(2) February 2, 2025 General Enforcement Unacceptable Risk Market Bans Strict European market prohibitions go into active effect. AI systems deemed as presenting unacceptable societal risks (e.g., social scoring, cognitive manipulation, facial biometric scraping) are permanently banned. Organizations must also begin workplace AI literacy training. Article 113(a) & Recital 179 May 2, 2025 EU Commission Codes of Practice Finalization The European AI Office drafts the primary Codes of Practice. These documents outline the expected operational compliance metrics for providers of General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models ahead of upcoming structural audits. Article 56(9) August 2, 2025 General Enforcement GPAI Model Rules & Governance Launch Regulatory frameworks activate. Obligations for General-Purpose AI (GPAI) model providers become legally binding. Rules regarding Notified Bodies (independent conformity assessment agencies), confidentiality provisions, and penalty rules also become active. Article 113(b) August 2, 2025 Businesses Legacy GPAI Transition Window Starts General-Purpose AI models that were already actively deployed or placed on the European market prior to August 2025 are granted a two-year transitional compliance runway, setting their ultimate compliance deadline to August 2, 2027. Article 111(3) August 2, 2025 Member States Designating National Supervisory Authorities Each EU member country must formally designate national competent authorities, identifying their respective notifying authorities and market surveillance authorities to handle local oversight and report to the central Commission. Article 70(2) August 2, 2025 Member States Fines & Penalty Systems Codification Member States must draft and formalize local penalty structures and administrative fine parameters to discipline violations of the regulation, communicating the implemented systems directly to the EU Commission. Recital 179 February 2, 2026 EU Commission High-Risk Post-Market Tracking Guidelines The European Commission publishes explicit operational guidelines clarifying high-risk AI system categorizations and setting post-market tracking parameters for providers of complex systems. Article 6(5) & Article 72(3) August 2, 2026 General Enforcement Annex III High-Risk Systems Application Enforcement extends to high-risk systems under Annex III. This triggers compliance protocols for biometrics, infrastructure, employment/HR, and law enforcement applications. Additionally, all Member States must establish at least one operational national sandbox. Article 113 & Article 57(1) August 2, 2027 General Enforcement Annex II Safety-Regulated AI Activation High-risk classification standards under Article 6(1) apply. This includes AI integrated as safety components of products already regulated under EU safety directives (e.g., medical equipment, industrial machinery, transportation safety devices). Article 113 August 2, 2027 Businesses Legacy GPAI Model Alignment Deadline The grace transition period expires. All legacy GPAI models on the market before August 2025 must now be fully compliant with transparency, documentation, and data-governance standards. Article 111(3) August 2, 2028 EU Commission AI Office Effectiveness Assessment The Commission completes a performance and governance evaluation of the European AI Office, analyzing institutional effectiveness. Concurrently, a progress review evaluates energy-efficient model standards and voluntary industry codes of conduct. Article 112(5) & Article 112(7) August 2, 2029 EU Commission First Structural Regulatory Review A comprehensive review of the AI Act is prepared for the European Parliament. This covers critical reassessments of Annex III high-risk boundaries, transparency measures, and the Commission's delegate powers to modify annexes. Article 112(3) & Article 97(2) August 2, 2030 General Enforcement Public Sector High-Risk AI Deadline High-risk AI systems implemented by public bodies and administrative agencies must reach complete compliance. Additionally, components of EU large-scale information platforms (Annex X) must be modernized to match the AI Act by December 31, 2030. Article 111(2) & Article 111(1) August 2, 2031 EU Commission Legislative Enforcement Performance Audit The European Commission presents its first formal performance audit on the practical enforcement of the AI Act to legislative authorities, concluding the multi-year implementation cycle with a comprehensive evaluation report.
